## Securities and Futures Commission Investment Products Department

## General Circular to SFC -approved Fund Management Companies

Subject:

Investment in SFC - authorised Real Estate Investment Trusts ('REITs') by  Unit  Trusts  and  Mutual  Funds  authorised  under  the  SFC  Code  on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds ('UT Code')

1. Pursuant to Chapter 7.14 of the UT Code, collective investment schemes authorised under  the  UT  Code  are  not allowed to  invest  in  any  type  of  real  estate  (including buildings) or interests in real estate (including options or rights but excluding shares in real estate companies).
2. Therefore, while a scheme authorised under Chapter 7 of the UT Code may invest up to 10% of its total net asset value in other collective investment schemes by way of Chapter 7.11 of the Code, it may not invest in  schemes that invest primarily in  real estate, generally known as real estate investment trusts ('REITs').
3. In  order  to  give  market  participants  more  flexibility,  the  SFC  has  reviewed  this investment restriction  and concluded that SFC-authorised REITs  should be  included as  a  type  of  permissible  collective  investment  scheme  under  Chapter  7.11  for  the following reasons:
4. (a)  All  SFC-authorised  REITs  are  required  to  be  listed  on  the  Stock  Exchange  of Hong Kong, therefore units in REITs can be readily bought and sold. Consequently, a collective investment scheme  that has  invested in  REITs would be able to dispose of  its  REIT units  on  the  stockmarket,  in  order  to  meet  any funding or redemption requirements.
5. (b) The  trading  of  SFC-authorised  REITs  on  the  stockmarket  helps to  ensure  that these investments are valued in a transparent, objective and timely manner.
4. SFC-authorised  REITs  are  now  permissible  collective  investment  schemes  under Chapter 7.11 of the UT Code with immediate effect.

Investment Products Department Securities and Futures Commission

4 November 2004
